signals.entity: NCR Atleos / Brink's (global OEM; Printec's key partner)
signals.country: UK (group-level; consequences across all 17 footprint countries)
signals.signal: The UK Competition and Markets Authority FORMALLY LAUNCHED its Phase 1 merger inquiry into Brink's ~USD 6.6bn acquisition of NCR Atleos on 26/08/2026, by notice to the parties, and set a statutory Phase 1 decision deadline of 22/10/2026. This is the material change since the last run: at 15/07/2026 the case was still only pre-Phase-1 (invitation to comment ran 20/05-04/06/2026) with no statutory clock. The CMA will now decide both whether the deal falls within the UK merger regime at all and whether it may substantially lessen competition; the deadline can be extended in limited circumstances.
signals.source_name: UK Competition and Markets Authority — case page, The Brink's Company / NCR Atleos Corporation merger inquiry
signals.implies: Printec's single most important supply relationship is now on a dated regulatory clock. The whole Printec ATM line — NCR dispense, intelligent-deposit and recycling hardware plus x-core multivendor software — sits behind a vendor that will be owned by Brink's, a company that already competes with Printec directly through Brink's Hellas (CIT plus full ATM Managed Services plus 'Brink's Complete' cash-as-a-service in Greece). Printec should use the 22/10/2026 date as the trigger for a formal channel conversation with Atleos EMEA: seek written confirmation that reseller and distribution terms, EMEA pricing and x-core interoperability survive the change of control, and quietly cost a multivendor fallback (Diebold Nixdorf or Hyosung hardware behind x-core) so that a Brink's-owned Atleos cannot squeeze the channel on renewal.
signals.likelihood: High that a Phase 1 decision issues by 22/10/2026; the outcome (clearance, undertakings-in-lieu, or Phase 2 referral) is genuinely open
signals.followup: Re-read the CMA case page in the week of 20/10/2026 for the Phase 1 decision and any commencement/issues papers; watch for a parallel EU or national filing, which has still not appeared in any footprint jurisdiction.

signals.entity: NCR Atleos (global OEM; Printec's key partner)
signals.signal: Atleos has PULLED IN its expected closing date for the Brink's transaction. CEO Tim Oliver in the Q2 release (05/08/2026): the regulatory and administrative processes 'are progressing and we now anticipate an accelerated timeline to close early in the first quarter of 2027.' The 10-Q filed the same day repeats that the Mergers 'are currently expected to close early in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals.' Prior guidance was simply 'Q1 2027'. Note the tension with the CMA clock above: a 22/10/2026 Phase 2 referral would make an early-Q1-2027 close very hard.
signals.source_name: NCR Atleos Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30/06/2026
signals.implies: Printec now has a workable planning date. Any NCR-based bid Printec is writing that will be delivered or renewed after Q1 2027 — Raiffeisen Serbia x-core, PrivatBank Ukraine recyclers, BCR APTRA, Erste Croatia OptiCash — should carry a change-of-control clause and price protection, because the counterparty behind the hardware and software will change owner inside the delivery window. It also sets the deadline for Printec to secure its EMEA partner terms in writing: after close, those terms get renegotiated by a competitor.
signals.likelihood: Close in early Q1 2027 is the companies' own stated expectation but is conditional on the CMA outcome
signals.followup: Track NCR Atleos 8-K and Brink's 8-K filings for the closing announcement and for any divestiture or behavioural undertaking offered to the CMA that touches EMEA ATM services.

signals.entity: NCR Atleos (global OEM; Printec's key partner)
signals.signal: Because of the pending Brink's transaction, Atleos DID NOT hold a Q2 2026 earnings conference call and DID NOT provide a financial outlook — stated explicitly in the release: 'In light of the pending transaction with The Brink's Company (Brink's), Atleos will not be hosting an earnings conference call to review second quarter results or providing a financial outlook.' The usual source of regional (EMEA/Europe) colour, ATMaaS endpoint counts and order-backlog commentary is therefore closed off for this quarter, and the written release contains no Europe or EMEA narrative at all — the only regional remarks are that Network volume growth came from South Africa and Australia.
signals.source_name: NCR Atleos Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1)
signals.implies: Printec should stop expecting to read its partner's EMEA intentions out of public disclosure until the deal closes, and switch to direct channel intelligence — the Atleos EMEA account team, the ATMIA and regional partner events, and Brink's own earnings call, which is still being held and now carries the combined story. Practically, this means Printec's competitive picture of its own supplier degrades for two to three quarters, which argues for putting the partner-terms conversation on the agenda now rather than waiting for guidance to resume.
signals.likelihood: Blackout persists until the transaction closes (companies' expectation: early Q1 2027)
signals.followup: Check whether Atleos resumes calls/outlook at Q3 2026 (release due ~early November 2026); if not, rely on Brink's quarterly call for combined-entity EMEA commentary.

signals.entity: NCR Atleos (global OEM; Printec's key partner)
signals.signal: The Q2 10-Q geographic disaggregation — a datapoint NOT in the scripted EDGAR segment series, which carries only total and reportable-segment revenue — shows EMEA revenue of USD 352m in Q2 2026 against USD 342m in Q2 2025 (+2.9%), and USD 666m for H1 2026 against USD 653m (+2.0%). EMEA is Atleos' second-largest region at roughly 32% of the USD 1,103m quarter, behind the US (USD 513m, +3.0%). Americas excluding the US fell sharply, from USD 144m to USD 120m (-16.7%); Asia Pacific was flat at USD 118m.
signals.source_name: NCR Atleos Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30/06/2026, revenue disaggregation by geography
signals.implies: EMEA is growing but only at low single digits, roughly in line with the US and well below the ATMaaS growth rate — which says the European book is still dominated by hardware and traditional maintenance rather than the as-a-service model. For Printec that is reassuring on volume (the NCR EMEA hardware pipeline it resells is stable, not shrinking) but it is also the number a Brink's-owned Atleos will be under pressure to accelerate, most obviously by converting EMEA bank fleets to Atleos-run ATMaaS — which is exactly the revenue Printec earns today through managed and field services. Printec should pre-empt this by leading with its own managed-service and telemetry/monitoring proposition at its NCR reference accounts rather than waiting to be disintermediated.
signals.likelihood: Continued low-single-digit EMEA growth with rising as-a-service mix is the visible trend
signals.followup: Re-key the EMEA geographic line from the Q3 2026 10-Q (due ~early November 2026) to see whether EMEA growth accelerates or decelerates as the deal closes.

signals.entity: NCR Atleos (global OEM; Printec's key partner)
signals.country: Group-level (ATMaaS applies across EMEA incl. footprint)
signals.signal: Q2 2026 operating metrics from the earnings release: revenue from ATMaaS arrangements was USD 77m, up from USD 62m a year earlier (+24%); Self-Service Banking annualised recurring revenue was USD 1,721m vs USD 1,679m; recurring revenue was 58% of Self-Service Banking revenue vs 57%. Against that, Network Managed Units were FLAT at 77.0 thousand (77.0k in both Q2 2026 and Q2 2025) and Network LTM ARPU edged down to USD 16.0k from USD 16.2k. Self-Service Banking Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% 'led by ATM as a Service, Software, net tariff refunds, and productivity initiatives offsetting elevated memory and fuel costs'; hardware revenue was described as 'steady at historically high 2025 levels'. ATMaaS — a model where the vendor owns and runs the bank's whole ATM estate, hardware, software, cash forecasting, servicing and monitoring, for a per-machine fee — remains the engine, while the owned independent ATM estate has stopped growing in unit terms.
signals.source_name: NCR Atleos Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1), 'Other performance metrics'
signals.implies: The flat 77.0k managed-unit count alongside +24% ATMaaS revenue tells Printec where the pressure will come from: Atleos is monetising deeper per machine and converting bank-owned fleets to service contracts rather than deploying more of its own ATMs. That is a direct substitute for what Printec sells as managed and field services, ATM telemetry and monitoring, and APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation — Atleos ATMaaS bundles cash forecasting into the fee. Printec's defensible answer at its NCR reference accounts (BCR, Erste Croatia, Raiffeisen Serbia, PrivatBank, OTP/Raiffeisen Albania) is the multivendor and local-service argument: x-core plus Printec field engineering keeps the bank hardware-agnostic and locally supported, where an Atleos ATMaaS contract locks the estate to one OEM at the moment that OEM is being bought by a CIT competitor.
signals.likelihood: ATMaaS conversion pressure on EMEA bank fleets intensifies through the close and after
signals.followup: Track the ATMaaS revenue line and Network Managed Units in the Q3 2026 release; ask the Atleos EMEA channel whether Printec can be an ATMaaS delivery partner rather than a displaced incumbent.

signals.entity: NCR Atleos / Cashzone (global OEM operating as an IAD in Printec's home market)
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 13/01/2026] Atleos announced that EPIRUS BANK selected it to modernise and expand the bank's ATM network across Greece under the ATMaaS model, using Cashzone network resources to give the bank a branded retail network. Atleos takes location selection, installation, maintenance and operational support; the ATMs carry Epirus Bank and Cashzone CO-BRANDING. Deployment began November 2025 with phased completion targeted in roughly three months (i.e. around February 2026). No unit count or contract value was disclosed. Cashzone is Atleos' own independent ATM deployer (IAD) brand — an operator that owns and runs ATMs in retail locations rather than for a bank — and Atleos states the Cashzone network runs 20,000 ATMs across Europe; Greece is a live Cashzone market (cashzone.gr). CORRECTION TO THE TRACKED POSITION: the roster entry for NCR Atleos records 'no NEW footprint ATMaaS/Cashzone win this window' — this Greek win was not captured and should be added. No fresher trigger on it was found in the 24/07-31/08/2026 delta window.
signals.source_name: NCR Atleos newsroom / investor press release, 'Epirus Bank Selects NCR Atleos to Modernize and Expand ATM Network Across Greece'
signals.implies: This is the concrete precedent that Printec's key partner will take a Greek bank's ATM estate directly, end to end, and brand it Cashzone — bypassing any integrator. Epirus Bank is a small cooperative-rooted lender, which is exactly the profile Printec would normally serve with NCR hardware plus x-core plus field service. Printec should treat the smaller and mid-tier Greek and Cypriot banks as at risk of the same pitch and get in front of them with a counter-offer: Printec-managed multivendor estate, ATM telemetry and monitoring, OptiCash cash optimisation and local engineering, positioned on the argument that co-branding an ATM 'Cashzone' hands the customer relationship and the retail siting decision to the vendor. It is also the template to watch for in Bulgaria, Romania and Croatia, where Cashzone-style IAD economics work.
signals.likelihood: Medium-to-high that Atleos repeats the Cashzone co-branded ATMaaS pitch at other small/mid footprint banks over 6-12 months
signals.followup: Confirm the deployed unit count and whether the phased rollout completed, via Greek press (capital.gr, ot.gr, naftemporiki.gr) and Epirus Bank's own site; check cashzone.gr for new bank co-branding in Greece and for any Cashzone entry into Bulgaria, Romania or Croatia.

signals.entity: Brink's (global; acquirer of Atleos and a direct Printec competitor via Brink's Hellas)
signals.country: Group-level, with direct Greek footprint exposure
signals.signal: Brink's Q2 2026 results (05/08/2026): revenue up 7% to USD 1.39bn, organic growth 4%, and ATM Managed Services plus Digital Retail Solutions (AMS/DRS) up 14% organically — the 14th consecutive quarter of mid-teens or better AMS/DRS organic growth — now representing over USD 1.5bn of trailing-twelve-month revenue and approaching a third of total revenue. Brink's confirmed the accelerated early-Q1-2027 close for Atleos and reiterated ~USD 200m of expected cost synergies, and introduced quarterly guidance framing mid-to-high-teens organic AMS/DRS growth for 2026. AMS is Brink's ATM outsourcing line; DRS is its retail cash-as-a-service line built on intelligent safes.
signals.source_name: Brink's press release, 'Brink's Delivers Strong Second-Quarter Results' (GlobeNewswire)
signals.implies: The acquirer's fastest-growing and highest-margin line is precisely ATM outsourcing — so the strategic logic of buying Atleos is to feed AMS with Atleos hardware, software and installed base. For Printec that converts an abstract ownership change into a concrete commercial threat in Greece, where Brink's Hellas already fields CIT plus full ATM Managed Services plus 'Brink's Complete', and can after close pitch a single contract covering the machine, the software, the cash and the servicing. Printec should assume its Greek and Cypriot ATM service revenue is the first target, and should differentiate on multivendor independence (x-core across mixed NCR/Diebold/Hyosung estates), on AML/KYC and transaction-monitoring adjacencies Brink's does not sell (Siron, FICO, INETCO, Thales HSM), and on Namirial eKYC — none of which a cash-logistics acquirer can bundle.
signals.likelihood: High that combined AMS+Atleos pressure lands in Greece first, then Romania, Croatia and Bulgaria
signals.followup: Listen to Brink's Q3 2026 call for the first explicit combined-entity EMEA/Europe ATM outsourcing plan; monitor Brink's Hellas for new Greek bank ATM outsourcing wins.

signals.entity: NCR Atleos x Sesami (global OEM; Sesami TCRs are a Printec-sold product line)
signals.country: United States only — watched for EMEA extension
signals.signal: RE-STATUS, no change: the Atleos reseller collaboration under which Atleos and its channel partners resell Sesami's CM-Series Intelligent Teller Cash Recycler to financial institutions, announced 23/06/2026, remains explicitly UNITED STATES ONLY. Atleos supports the devices with its US field-service organisation. A targeted search of the Atleos newsroom and investor releases through 31/08/2026 found NO announcement extending the Sesami collaboration to EMEA or Europe. A TCR (teller cash recycler) is a branch counter machine that accepts, authenticates, stores and re-dispenses the same banknotes, removing manual cash handling from the teller.
signals.source_name: NCR Atleos investor press release, 'NCR Atleos Establishes U.S. Reseller Collaboration with Sesami for CM-Series Intelligent Teller Cash Recycler Solutions'
signals.implies: Printec resells Sesami TCRs alongside Glory in its cash-automation line, so an Atleos-Sesami reseller arrangement extended into EMEA would put Printec's partner into direct channel conflict with Printec on the same box at the same banks — Bank of Cyprus (Glory TCR) and the branch-automation pipeline generally. For now it stays US-only and is NOT a live footprint threat, but it is the single clearest early-warning indicator to keep watching: Printec should raise territorial exclusivity for Sesami CM-Series in its 17 countries directly with Sesami now, while Atleos is distracted by the merger, rather than after a Brink's-owned Atleos decides to globalise the arrangement.
signals.likelihood: Low-to-medium that an EMEA extension is announced within 12 months; rises materially after the Brink's close
signals.followup: Watch the Atleos and Sesami newsrooms for any territorial extension; open a direct conversation with Sesami on footprint territorial terms.

coverage_notes: Fresh run (no prior checkpoint for 2026-08-31). Primary-source first throughout. Opened: the UK CMA case page (the decisive item this run - Phase 1 formally launched 26/08/2026, statutory deadline 22/10/2026, upgrading the previous run's 'pre-Phase-1, no statutory clock' status); NCR Atleos Q2 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K EX-99.1, 05/08/2026) and Form 10-Q for Q2 (accession 0001974138-26-000016), both pulled directly from EDGAR; the EDGAR submissions index for CIK 1974138 to enumerate all filings since May 2026; the Atleos newsroom (ncratleos.com/news) and investor press-release archive; the Epirus Bank Greece ATMaaS/Cashzone release; the Sesami TCR reseller release; cashzone.gr; and Brink's Q2 2026 release via GlobeNewswire. Per rule 9 I did NOT re-key total revenue or reportable segments (already in intel-cache/competitor_series.json); what I captured instead is the JUDGMENT layer plus two disclosure items the script does not hold: the geographic revenue disaggregation (EMEA USD 352m Q2, USD 666m H1) and the operating metrics (ATMaaS revenue USD 77m, SSB ARR USD 1,721m, Network Managed Units flat at 77.0k). GENUINE GAPS, stated honestly: (1) There is NO Q2 EMEA or Europe narrative to report, because Atleos cancelled its earnings call and withheld guidance for the pending merger - I have filed that suppression itself as a signal rather than pretending commentary exists, and no ATMaaS endpoint count or order-backlog figure is publicly disclosed anywhere for EMEA. Do not expect anyone to produce one this quarter. (2) NO new footprint win, loss, launch or country entry by Atleos was found in the 24/07-31/08/2026 delta window. I searched the Atleos newsroom (its May-August 2026 output is entirely US credit-union and thought-leadership content), plus targeted local-language and multi-country sweeps for Romania/Bulgaria/Serbia/Croatia/Hungary and a Greek-language sweep on Epirus Bank/Cashzone - all negative. That absence is a finding, not a gap in effort. (3) The one genuinely new footprint discovery is a CORRECTION rather than a delta-window event: the Epirus Bank Greece Cashzone co-branded ATMaaS win (13/01/2026) was NOT in the tracked roster position, which asserted no footprint Cashzone win; it is filed as [STANDING - dated 13/01/2026] per the recency rule, flagged is_new for the changed position, and NOT presented as new news. Its deployed unit count is undisclosed and unverified. (4) Cashzone country count: Atleos' own Italy release states 20,000 ATMs across Europe and Italy as the thirteenth country; the roster's fourteenth (Colombia, 21/05/2026) is non-footprint. No new Cashzone country entry this window. (5) Lloyds Banking Group's Atleos ATMaaS/coin-recycling innovation-branch pilot (Manchester and Glasgow) dates to July 2025, is UK non-footprint and has no fresh trigger, so it is deliberately NOT filed as a signal. (6) COMESA's Competition Commission has a parallel notice of inquiry into the same acquisition (case CCC/MER/05/25/2026, status 'under assessment'), but its jurisdiction is Eastern and Southern Africa, entirely outside the footprint, and the notice PDF carries no visible dates - not filed as a signal. No EU or national merger filing in any footprint jurisdiction was visible anywhere. (7) One minor 10-Q item noted and not filed: Atleos disclosed immaterial prior-period misstatements relating to subscription software revenue recognition, certain network revenue and costs, and indirect-tax remeasurement - not Printec-relevant. All eight signals capped at Medium confidence per rule 3.

Resolved per the access protocol by retrying the SAME primary URL with curl and a desktop Chrome User-Agent plus a contact e-mail (SEC requires an identifying UA); the release and the 10-Q were then extracted and de-tagged locally. Nothing was dropped. 2) First 10-Q fetch attempt used the 8-K accession folder (0001974138-26-000014) and returned a 217-byte stub; resolved by reading the EDGAR submissions JSON (data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001974138.json) to get the correct 10-Q accession 0001974138-26-000016. 3) fintechfutures.com returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch on the Lloyds/Atleos article; not escalated further because the item proved to be July 2025, non-footprint and out of scope, and the substance was available from the Atleos investor release. 4) comesacompetition.org served the case-registry page but the underlying Website-Notice-Brink-NCR.pdf carries no dates in the rendered page; not escalated, non-footprint jurisdiction. 5) cashzone.gr/en/about is pure marketing copy and publishes NO ATM count, partner-bank list or launch date - the Greek Cashzone estate size remains unquantified and I have not estimated it. 6) No paywall blocked anything material this run; the MLex article on the CMA probe is subscription-only but the CMA case page itself is the better primary source and was fully readable.

The one document an operator could usefully retrieve if a deeper read is wanted is the CMA's Commencement Notice PDF (89KB) linked from the CMA case page at https://www.gov.uk/cma-cases/the-brinks-company-slash-ncr-atleos-corporation-merger-inquiry, which may name the specific UK product markets under review (ATM hardware, ATM managed services, cash logistics) and thereby indicate whether any remedy would touch EMEA ATM services; it is public, not gated.
